gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-sarala: Expressive, with letters strung like beads and no thinning, Bruno Ace SC leads. Sarala, a plain sans with neon-tube thickness, sits beside it like a friendly glow after a loud one.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-shippori-antique-: Bruno Ace SC strings out wide, open letters with no thinning. Shippori Antique B1 is a sans-serif with daylight through every curve, and that shared openness is what ties the two together.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-snippet: Beaded display letters up top, with no thinning anywhere in Bruno Ace SC. And Snippet, a plain sans with a crescent-wrench c, keeps paragraphs moving with a wiry, friendly lilt.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-tasa-explorer: Ribbon-cut letters, constant in width, march across the line in Bruno Ace SC, each one spaced like a bead. The first makes statements; TASA Explorer, a sans, makes sense of paragraphs.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-titillium-web: Uniform-stroke display letters, all one thickness, lead in Bruno Ace SC. Titillium Web, a plain sans with stroke ends set far apart, shares that spaciousness, which is what makes the pair hang together.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-tsukimi-rounded: Bruno Ace SC strings its letters like beads on a long thread, open throughout and free of calligraphic thinning. Tsukimi Rounded, a sans-serif, mirrors that openness with round, parenthesis-like forms.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-tuffy: Beads on a thread: that is Bruno Ace SC. Tuffy, a plain sans drawn as if by a pencil that never presses harder, shares that openness, down to a widely parted s.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-varela: Varela, a sans-serif with a wide-mouthed c and a t of one width, is the friendly one. But Bruno Ace SC, with its beaded spacing, is the one built to make an entrance.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-wix-madefor-displ: No hairlines, just open letters strung like beads on a thread. Bruno Ace SC is built for that kind of statement, while Wix Madefor Display, a sans-serif with gently flared curve ends, handles the quieter lines.
gen-gf-bruno-ace-sc-gf-ysabeau-infant: Bruno Ace SC strings out open letters with no pressure swells to slow the eye. Ysabeau Infant, a sans with terminals that point outward like tongs, shares that frank, open manner.
